label: PLAN 04
prompt:
BEGIN PROMPT

PLAN 04 | A BLACK MASS ENTERS THE HARBOR
DURATION 15 SECONDS | HORIZONTAL 16:9

CHARACTER REFERENCES
{{CHAR_SHIP_CREW}}

LOCATION REFERENCES
{{LOC_HARBOR_APPROACH}}
{{LOC_WORKING_QUAY}}

PROP REFERENCES
{{PROP_ZAHHAK_SHIP}}
{{PROP_MERCHANT_BOATS}}

DIRECTION AND CONTINUITY
Create a 15-second horizontal 16:9 live-action cinematic sequence.

Preserve the referenced ship’s exact silhouette, immense scale, advanced engineered construction, black materials and snake-headed structural details. These are serpent heads, not dragon heads.

Preserve each referenced character’s costume, proportions and rigid handmade mask. All visible humans wear their referenced masks.

Each listed hard cut changes the physical camera position and viewpoint.

References anchor design; the written lighting controls illumination.

NO MUSIC.
NO DIALOGUE.

LOCATION AND LIGHT
Full night at the harbor.

Sparse cold practical lights from the port skim the immense black hull. Small recessed ship lights reveal functional edges, railings and structural serpent motifs.

In Shot 1, a dense bank of natural sea fog occupies the harbor entrance behind and around the approaching bow. The foreground water and the nearest quay remain clearer.

Fragments of the island city, quay walls and scattered harbor lamps remain visible at the extreme left and right edges of the frame. Keep the central approach dominated by fog and the emerging ship.

The fog is uneven and physically drifting. It does not glow or open symmetrically.

As the ship reaches the clearer water beside the quay in Shots 2 and 3, the dense fog remains farther behind it at the harbor entrance. Preserve the same night exposure and lighting direction.

START STATE AND BLOCKING
Zahhak’s dedicated ship approaches bow-first from the fog-covered harbor entrance toward the camera and the quay at slow docking speed.

Its forward movement is already underway when the sequence begins.

At the opening frame, the snake-headed bow ornament is just beginning to become visible through the fog. Most of the hull remains concealed behind it.

Ordinary merchant vessels remain much smaller beside the quay.

SHOT 04-01 | 0s–3s | 3 SECONDS
12mm extreme wide from the shore, close to water height, looking toward the harbor entrance.

Keep the camera nearly fixed.

The snake-headed structure at the tip of the bow emerges first from the dense sea fog near the center of the frame.

Immediately behind it, the immense black bow becomes progressively visible as the ship advances toward the camera at slow docking speed.

Reveal the front of the hull through its actual forward movement: first the serpent head, then the bow’s sharp silhouette, then the broad dark surfaces rising behind it.

The ship is already close to the front edge of the fog bank; this is a short continuous emergence, not a distant ship suddenly racing across the harbor.

Trailing fog remains around the upper structure and behind the hull. Do not clear the entire ship within this shot.

The approaching bow grows slightly larger and pushes a heavy displacement wave across the foreground water.

Fragments of quay walls, small merchant craft and harbor lamps remain visible along the far left and right edges. These fixed elements establish the ship’s overwhelming scale.

No zoom.
No speed ramp.
No magical fog reveal.

Hard cut while the black mass is still advancing out of the fog.

SHOT 04-02 | 3s–11s | 8 SECONDS
18mm very low angle from the quay beside the approaching hull.

The bow and flank extend beyond the top and side of the frame.

Track slowly along the quay for one meter as recessed lights and snake-shaped structural details pass overhead.

Small masked crew members work at the upper rail.

Keep the immense flank moving across the frame.

SHOT 04-03 | 11s–15s | 4 SECONDS
24mm from a new quay station directly below the upper command landing, sharply looking upward.

Recessed deck lights reveal small masked crew against the immense black engineered structure.

Tilt slowly up from a snake-headed structural brace to the landing.

No dragon heads.

Prepare the elevated authority without bringing Zahhak down to the quay.

END STATE AND EDIT
The ship has reached docking position.

A deliberate short ellipse may complete mooring before the next block.

Keep ship design, night exposure and elevated landing consistent.

SOUND
Heavy low machinery, displaced water, hull creaks and metal tension.

Keep the machinery physically localized to the ship, not a musical drone.

No dramatic impact accompanies the emergence from the fog.

NO MUSIC.
NO DIALOGUE.

END PROMPT

Established requirements for this subject:
- No human appears without a mask. Every person on screen, including nobles, gift-bearers, servants and background figures, wears a mask. A figure who is not a named character takes one of the masked caste looks in REF-001, Civilization Caste Board. Never show a bare human face.

<<<image_2>>> is Palace Guards (GRP-005 V01); match it wherever Palace Guards appears.
<<<image_3>>> is China Port Panorama (LOC-036 V02); match it wherever China Port Panorama appears.
<<<image_4>>> is China Port Night Dock (LOC-038 V01); match it wherever China Port Night Dock appears.
<<<image_5>>> is Zahhak Ship (PRP-024 V02); match it wherever Zahhak Ship appears.
